# Proctor House Rottweilers

> Premium marketing/conversion site for an Arizona Rottweiler breeder ("Designer Gorilla" bloodline) — converts an existing social audience into waitlist applications and deposits.

## Project Overview

**Tech Stack:** Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack) · React 19 · TypeScript · Tailwind CSS v4 · next/font (Cinzel/Anton/Inter)
**Status:** Phase 1.5 complete — real client content, merch storefront, passcode-gated buyer portal. Deployed to Vercel, still behind Vercel Authentication. Payload CMS/Postgres/R2/Stripe in later phases
**Purpose:** Paid client project; the client is non-technical and will self-manage content via CMS in Phase 2

## Core Documentation

- `proctor-house-rottweilers-website-spec.md` — Client-approved spec; source of truth for scope/phases

## Key Files by Area

### Data (the CMS seam — most load-bearing module)
- `src/lib/placeholder-data.ts` — all types, records, brand constants, selectors, `vitalCells()`/`formatDate()`/`formatPrice()`. Phase 2 swaps records for Payload queries; types stay

### Access control
- `src/lib/litter-access.ts` — **server-only.** Passcode verification + signed cookie. Read the header comment first

### Design system
- `src/app/globals.css` — Tailwind v4 @theme tokens, gold-metallic gradient, font-plate/font-impact utilities
- `src/app/layout.tsx` — fonts, metadata, chrome composition

### Pages
- `src/app/page.tsx` — Home (hero → plates → litters → social → #waitlist)
- `src/app/dogs/page.tsx` — Our Dogs index (foundation + next-generation teasers)
- `src/app/dogs/[slug]/page.tsx` — dog detail; static params filtered to foundation dogs
- `src/app/shop/page.tsx` — merch catalogue + documented Stripe seam
- `src/app/litters/[slug]/page.tsx` — public litter page
- `src/app/litters/[slug]/updates/` — passcode-gated buyer portal (dynamic)
- `src/app/the-bloodline/page.tsx`, `src/app/about/page.tsx`

### Components
- `src/components/BloodlinePlate.tsx` — signature gold-framed dog card (foundation + teaser states)
- `src/components/{VitalsStrip,HealthCertificate,PedigreePanel}.tsx` — dog profile panels
- `src/components/{ShirtMockup,PhotoPlaceholder}.tsx` — drawn placeholders for missing assets
- `src/components/{Nav,Footer,WaitlistCta,Hero,Reveal,SocialEmbed}.tsx`

## Common Tasks

**To run locally:** `npm run dev` (port 3000; `.claude/launch.json` has the preview config)
**To add/edit a dog:** edit `dogs` in `src/lib/placeholder-data.ts`; plates, index and detail page update together
**To add a litter with a portal:** add the `Litter` record with `updatesEnabled: true` and a `passcodeEnvKey`, then set that env var in Vercel and redeploy
**To verify:** `npx tsc --noEmit && npm run lint && npm run build`
**To check the portal is still gated:** confirm `/litters/[slug]/updates` shows as `ƒ (Dynamic)` in build output
**Before touching Next.js APIs:** read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` — this Next version has breaking changes vs. training data (see AGENTS.md)

## Environment Variables

See `.env.example`. Local values go in `.env.local` (gitignored); production values in Vercel.

- `LITTER_ACCESS_SECRET` — cookie signing key. Must be the **output** of the generator command (~43 chars, no spaces), not the command itself. Rotating it revokes every buyer's access
- `LITTER_PASSCODE_KINGS`, `LITTER_PASSCODE_CINEMA` — per-litter buyer codes. 10+ chars, no pattern between them, never derived from anything in this repo
- Later: Payload secret, DATABASE_URL (Neon), R2 keys, Stripe keys (client-owned; never handled by the developer — ADR-003)

## Hard Constraints

- **Never publish an unredacted certificate scan.** `/images` holds originals with owner name, registration and microchip numbers and is gitignored. Anything in `public/pedigrees/` must be redacted in the pixels and checked by eye (ADR-007)
- **Never display a health clearance the client doesn't hold.** Missing vitals render as "—" (ADR-006)
- **The buyer portal is deterrence, not authentication.** No rate limiting; nothing sensitive goes behind it (ADR-008)
- **This repo is public.** No secrets, no plausible example passcodes, not even in comments
- Mobile is the primary experience; the persistent waitlist CTA must survive all changes
